clue.text: The sure thing?

blocks.note: sure means certain, definite
an article is an item or thing

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bet or plan is a certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sure thing' reads as a bet on a certainty, but 'The' is the word being defined and the rest builds its grammatical name; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'the' is the definite article, contrasted with the indefinite a or an.

clue.text: Made poorly by oppressive climate?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone falls ill because of muggy, heavy conditions
setter's reading: the idiom for feeling unwell, taken literally as being pressed down beneath the skies

explanation.surface: A person blames a sticky, sultry spell for making them ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means slightly unwell; the clue pretends the phrase is literal, with the oppressive climate sitting on top of the sufferer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means feeling slightly ill, which is what 'made poorly' describes, poorly being British for unwell.

clue.text: Summer garden visitor has scarlet and navy head

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red
an admiral is the head of a navy

explanation.surface: A colourful visitor to a garden in summer wears a scarlet and navy cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the top of the visitor's body, but 'navy head' is a naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral is a common butterfly that feeds on garden flowers such as buddleia in summer.

clue.text: Employment of smaller number's serving no purpose

blocks.note: employment of something is its use
a smaller amount or number is less

explanation.surface: A dry remark that employing fewer people achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless has no function, so it serves no purpose.

clue.text: Threaten conflict with North

blocks.note: war is armed conflict
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: A nation menaces another with war on its northern border.
explanation.definitionFit: To warn someone can mean to threaten them with consequences, as in a warning shot.

clue.text: Pension off landlord after overwork and hate mail

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word that follows is read from its end to its start
off suggests something gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a work is an OP, short for opus, and over turns it round
taken as written, to be rearranged
a landlord is one who lets property, a letter

explanation.surface: A tenant pensioned off by a landlord after overwork responds with hate mail.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in a different order from the clue: overwork comes first, then the rearranged pension, with the landlord placed 'after' them. A letter, cryptically, is anyone who lets.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison-pen letter is an anonymous, malicious message, a classic form of hate mail.

clue.text: Childbirth with fashionable pain relief machine, I've found to be hard work

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, 'requiring much work', fitting 'to be hard work'

blocks.note: labour is the process of childbirth
something in is fashionable
a TENS machine relieves pain with small electrical pulses, often used in labour
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A mother reports that giving birth, even with a trendy pain-relief gadget, was exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: TENS (transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation) units are commonly offered to women in labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A labour-intensive task demands a lot of effort and manpower, so it is hard work.

clue.text: Tight-woven dress has no end of curves

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the following word is cut off
woven threads are interlaced and crossed, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: tight with money is mean
taken as written, then shortened and mixed

explanation.surface: A closely woven dress lacks any curvy shaping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight-woven' reads as one fabric adjective, but the hyphen splits into a synonym and an anagram signal; 'no end of curves' sounds like many curves, yet the definition is the verb at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A river or path that meanders winds and curves this way and that.

clue.text: Second ballot gets 5-0 to overrule declaration

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the next word
over means turned over, so the word that follows is read backwards

blocks.note: the second letter of ballot
5 is V in Roman numerals, and 0 looks like the letter O
a rule is a LAW, and over turns it round

explanation.surface: A rerun vote passes unanimously, five to nothing, overturning an earlier announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overrule' is one word in the surface but splits into a reversal signal and 'rule'.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open statement or admission, a formal declaration of something.

clue.text: Film part of Medicine Man's taken by Sean Connery

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a section taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A scene from the 1992 film Medicine Man, which starred Sean Connery.
explanation.walkthrough: Medicine Man really is a Sean Connery film, so the last words only colour the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema means film as an art form or industry, as in 'French cinema'.

clue.text: Yearns to be sexy? Fat chance!

blocks.note: to yearn is to long
hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: Someone longs to be attractive and is told it will never happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like a jibe at the dreamer's figure, but 'Fat chance' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is something with little likelihood of success, which is what 'fat chance' sarcastically means.

clue.text: Handle strike infiltrated by Left

indicators.note: something infiltrated has another thing slipped inside it

blocks.note: to strike is to hit
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Industrial action undermined by left-wing activists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout and 'Left' a political wing; both are simple synonyms here.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilt is the handle of a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Evangelist girl on Scottish isle steals everyone's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only the middle letters are kept

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
the two central letters of everyone

explanation.surface: A charming preacher girl on a Hebridean island wins over the whole community.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is fitting: St Columba founded a monastery there to spread Christianity in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A missionary spreads a religious faith, as an evangelist does.

clue.text: Doomed by injuries on pitch, the German''s withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: ills are harms or injuries
pitch is a black tarry substance
der is a form of 'the' in German

explanation.surface: A football team's chances are ruined by injuries on the pitch, and their German player has pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is the black sticky stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-starred is born under an unlucky star, so they are doomed to misfortune.

clue.text: Vicar plays lyre at festivities

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it and moving its parts around

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The parish vicar strums a lyre at a village celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plays' looks like a musician playing the lyre, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is lively, noisy merrymaking, the stuff of festivities.

clue.text: Feeling bad about running away

indicators.note: bad means gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone regrets having run off.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeing is escaping from danger, which is running away.

clue.text: Urges to have punch in dedicated containers

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
punch is a mixed drink, and a cup is another such drink

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to serve punch in special containers.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup is a mixed fruity drink, like claret cup or Pimm's, as punch is. 'Dedicated' means made for one purpose: an egg cup holds only eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg cups are small containers made specifically to hold a boiled egg, so they are single-purpose.

clue.text: Environmentally friendly lamp gets go-ahead

blocks.note: green means eco-friendly
a lamp is a light

explanation.surface: An energy-saving lamp receives approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A green light is permission to proceed, from traffic signals, so it is the go-ahead.

clue.text: Made up German song?

blocks.note: first meaning: told untruths, invented a story
second meaning: a German art song, as by Schubert

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a composer inventing a song; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of telling falsehoods and the German term for a romantic art song.

clue.text: Famous hotel is to have Royal in charge

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO alphabet
taken as written
taken as written
R is an abbreviation for Royal
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A celebrated hotel is to be run by a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means notable in history, so famous and important in the past.

clue.text: Huge bird mangled hare

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A giant bird of prey has torn a hare apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Conduct another trial at New Street

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are formed into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A court case is reheard at a venue called New Street.
explanation.walkthrough: New Street is a real name, Birmingham's main railway station, so 'New' reads as part of an address.
explanation.definitionFit: To retest is to test again, which is to carry out a further trial.

clue.text: Claim to find support in beer?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: A drinker claims to find comfort in a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, which is to claim it.

clue.text: Quietly hoard jam

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a hoard is a store kept in reserve

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly stockpiles jars of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoard' and 'jam' both look like verbs, but jam is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserve is a noun for fruit boiled with sugar, which is jam.
